sampling_model.design: Independent observations from \(P_Q\), with a deterministic three-way sample split and known uniform covariate design on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\).
sampling_model.treatment: Binary observational treatment with conditional ignorability and \(\kappa\le\pi_Q(x)\le1-\kappa\).
sampling_model.overlap: Uniform overlap is fixed over \(\mathcal X\); the full class also has a positive density band around \(x_0\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Private tensor-spline sufficient-statistic releases for \(\pi_Q\) and \(\mu_{0,Q}\), followed by Hölder-ball projection; a separate block supplies the privatized linear and quadratic local moments.
sampling_model.privacy: Replacement \((\epsilon_n,\delta_n)\)-differential privacy under parallel composition across disjoint blocks, a single joint Gaussian release within each block, and post-processing for stabilization and interval formation.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The higher-order local-polynomial learner attains the privacy-free pointwise CATE minimax rate under its regularity conditions.
Worst-case bias-aware local-polynomial confidence intervals are honest and shrink at the optimal nonparametric rate.
A doubly robust uniform confidence band is constructed for a lower-dimensional CATE function under nonprivate sampling.
DP-CATE preserves Neyman orthogonality asymptotically and gives quasi-oracle conditions for private two-stage CATE learners.
Theorem 4.6 constructs a valid private interval for the population ATE from private point and variance estimates.
A black-box resampling framework converts a private estimator into an asymptotically valid and tight nonparametric confidence interval.

body.tldr: The paper constructs replacement-private, finite-sample honest pointwise CATE intervals on the uniform-design attainable class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\).  The higher-order interval clips its released center to \([-1,1]\) before adding the deterministic radius, so it is a nonempty random interval on every transcript; projection cannot increase error from the bounded CATE target.  It achieves \(1\wedge r_{\mathrm{up}}\), while the fixed-dimensional direct-regression interval proved on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}\) remains valid after restriction to \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\).  A public selector therefore gives the attainable-class upper \(C\min\{1\wedge r_{\mathrm{up}},1\wedge[n^{-\beta/(2\beta+d)}\vee N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-\beta/(\beta+d)}]\}\); the same uniform-design witness used for the ordinary full-class lower belongs to the attainable class, yielding the corresponding two-sided nonsharp bracket.  On the unchanged full class, only the separate ordinary \(\gamma\)-smooth lower and \(\beta\)-smooth direct-regression upper are certified, and the exact private confidence frontier remains open.

project_justification.gap: Private CATE papers provide point releases or quasi-oracle guarantees, and private causal interval papers treat regular average effects. They do not give a uniform pointwise Hölder CATE coverage theorem that accounts simultaneously for higher-order nuisance bias, sampling uncertainty, privacy composition, and privacy noise.
project_justification.niche: A bias-aware fixed-length construction on a fixed KBRW-attainable positive-density submodel permits honest nonregular causal inference without assuming the desired coverage or length and without relying on the rejected paired-microcell lower bound.
project_justification.fill: The project privatizes every pilot and localized moment for the attainable higher-order construction, clips the released center before interval formation, and proves unrestricted-finite-rank concentration, transcript-wise nonemptiness, uniform finite-sample coverage, and the phase-sensitive mean interval length upper \(1\wedge r_{\mathrm{up}}\) on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\).  It also proves a fixed-dimensional direct-regression interval on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}\), which restricts to the attainable class.  Combining the two by a public deterministic selector and observing that the ordinary lower-bound witness itself has uniform design gives the best certified attainable-class bracket: under \(L_\pi\ge\kappa\), \(\delta_n\le c_0/n\), and sufficiently large \(n\), its lower endpoint is \(c[n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}\vee\{1\wedge(n\epsilon_n)^{-\gamma/(\gamma+d)}\}]\) and its upper endpoint is \(C\min\{1\wedge r_{\mathrm{up}},1\wedge[n^{-\beta/(2\beta+d)}\vee N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-\beta/(\beta+d)}]\}\).  Separately, the unchanged full class retains its nonsharp ordinary lower versus direct-regression upper bracket; the attainable higher-order upper is not transferred back to that class, and exact full-class sharpness remains unresolved.

body.related_work: Kennedy, Balakrishnan, Robins, and Wasserman (2024) establish the privacy-free pointwise CATE rate and motivate the higher-order local-polynomial architecture.  Their upper theorem requires its stated design-density and population-Gram conditions; this paper verifies the needed higher-order identities only for its uniform-design attainable construction and does not assert that the KBRW upper transfers to \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}\).  Nor is KBRW's density-hole fuzzy lower asserted to transfer to the present full class with a positive anchor density band.  On \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\), the paper instead combines its private higher-order interval with its fixed-dimensional direct-regression interval and proves an ordinary two-law lower using witnesses that are themselves uniform-design attainable laws.  The resulting attainable-class bracket is nonsharp but can strictly improve the higher-order upper through deterministic selection.  The separate full-class result remains the ordinary \(\gamma\)-smooth lower versus the \(\beta\)-smooth direct-regression upper.  Robins, Li, Tchetgen Tchetgen, and van der Vaart (2008) supply the higher-order influence-function perspective behind the attainable quadratic correction.  Armstrong and Kolesár (2020) motivate honest fixed-length intervals that expose worst-case smoothing bias.  Lee, Okui, and Whang (2017) provide nonprivate doubly robust CATE bands in a lower-dimensional heterogeneity problem.  Schröder, Melnychuk, and Feuerriegel (2025) study private orthogonal CATE learning but do not derive this pointwise Hölder coverage and length phase; Schröder, Hartenstein, and Feuerriegel (2025) treat private intervals for the regular population ATE.  Shoham, Shenfeld, Velner-Harris, and Ligett (2026) give an asymptotic resampling conversion for private estimators, whereas the present intervals use explicit uniform finite-sample bias control.  Dwork and Roth (2014) provide the Gaussian mechanism and post-processing fact used by both private constructions.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The higher-order privacy term comes from the global sensitivity \(m^{-1}(h^{-d}+kh^{-2d})\) of the clipped quadratic-moment release and is proved only as an attainable-submodel upper cost.  The separate full-class direct-regression release has sensitivity \(O((nh^d)^{-1})\) but incurs armwise bias \(O(h^\beta)\), so it does not determine whether the smoother \(\gamma\)-contrast, the nuisance interaction \(q\), or a stabilized private Gram controls the sharp frontier.  The invalid paired-microcell transport step is not revived.
body.honest_scope: Settled results are replacement privacy and uniform finite-sample coverage of the explicit clipped-center higher-order interval on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\), including its nonemptiness on every transcript, its achieved length upper \(1\wedge r_{\mathrm{up}}\), the corrected construction-specific privacy-free reduction with no rank floor, and the attainable-class nonsharp minimax bracket obtained by taking the better of that interval and the restricted direct-regression interval.  The bracket's lower witness has uniform design and satisfies every attainable assumption.  The attainable class remains a restricted submodel; its higher-order upper is not transferred to \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}\).  On the full class, the settled results are the ordinary lower limitation and the fixed-dimensional direct-regression coverage and upper bound, giving \(c[n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}\vee\{1\wedge(n\epsilon_n)^{-\gamma/(\gamma+d)}\}]\le\mathcal L_n^*(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}})\le C[1\wedge\{n^{-\beta/(2\beta+d)}\vee N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-\beta/(\beta+d)}\}]\) under \(L_\pi\ge\kappa\), \(\delta_n\le c_0/n\), and sufficiently large \(n\).  Whether either bracket is tight, including whether a \(q\)-driven or private-Gram branch is unavoidable, remains unresolved; in particular, the full-class OEQ stays open.
